To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the alternative splicing of a suboptimal intraexonic splice site is dependent on the splicing of constitutive introns upstream; and 2) the length of the constitutive introns plays a key role in the splicing of the intra-exonic alternative intron.

the alternative splicing of the TPO gene depends on the assembly of the constitutive introns spliceosome and on the qualitative scanning of the alternative introns sequence by the transcription/splicing complex.

the alternative splicing of the last exon of the human TPO gene is regulated by a mechanism that is dependent on the assembly of the splicing machinery complex on upstream constitutive intron(s) and that is influenced by the length of the intron to be spliced and by the quality of its splice sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular mechanisms underlying the alternative splicing of the last exon of the human thrombopoiesis gene.
the molecular mechanism of alternative splicing and with the regulation of this process by upstream introns in the TPO minigenes.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying alternative splicing of the thrombopoiesis gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alternative splicing of the TPO gene requires the splicing machinery to scan the sequence and to find the best splice sites.
the alternative intron is not spliced out in the absence of upstream constitutive exons, and that it is not spliced in the presence of upstream exons.

the alternative splicing of the TPO gene depends on the presence of the upstream intron and the suboptimal nature of the alternative intronic sequence, which in turn are both necessary for the recognition of the alternative introns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alternative splicing of the 116 nt alternative TPO intron requires the splicing of the constitutive upstream intron, which is a common mechanism for the recognition of suboptimally spliced exons.

the recognition of the TPO alternative intron depends on the presence of constitutive introns upstream of the alternative intronic region, and that the alternative intron is a suboptimal splice site that can be recognized only when the spliceosome complex is primed by upstream introns.
the alternative splicing of a constitutive intron can be a mechanism to enhance the recognition of sub-optimal splice sites in a gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

alternative intron splicings are not always the result of a competition between alternative splicing regulatory elements, as it has been proposed for other genes, but can also be the result of an interplay between the splicing machinery and the sequence context of the splicing signals.
the presence of upstream introns is necessary to promote efficient splicing of the alternative intronic sequence, which otherwise would be spliced out at a very low rate.

the splicing process is not a simple and sequential mechanism of introns removal, but a more complex and dynamic process, where the recognition of sub-optimal splice sites is influenced by the presence of upstream splice sites.
